confidence_note: The old TR text's '20-25% IQ correlation' and 'EQ earns more' claims could not be tied to the book and are dropped. Kept: the three-trait frame (IQ, personality, EQ), EQ as the flexible one, the 58% and 90% figures and the four skills, all confirmed by several summaries and TalentSmart's own papers. The figures come from the authors' company TalentSmart, not independent research; the story must say so. The '70% average-IQ people outperform high-IQ people' claim appears in one summary only and is left out. No concrete scene in the book for this concept; no example is invented.
facts: Bradberry and Greaves name three traits that shape a person: IQ, personality and emotional intelligence (EQ).
They say IQ and personality are largely fixed, while EQ is flexible and can be built with practice.
They state that EQ explains 58% of success in job performance across all types of jobs.
They state that 90% of top performers are high in EQ.
These figures come from TalentSmart, the authors' own company, which tests EQ; they are not independent research.
They split EQ into four skills: self-awareness and self-management (about oneself), social awareness and relationship management (about others).
The book includes a passcode to an online EQ appraisal that scores the four skills and points to which of its 66 strategies would help most.
tension: A single number says IQ is not what separates good performers, yet the number comes from the authors' own company.
opening_idea: Start with the number 58 and what it supposedly explains.

lessons.idea: Treat the skills that can change as the place to put effort, and keep the headline figures at the weight of their source.
lessons.anchor: IQ and personality largely fixed, EQ flexible; 58% from TalentSmart's own data.

reflect_final: Of the four skills, which one would the people who work with you say you use least, and what would you try first in the coming week?

use_cases.situation: A colleague is sure that talent is fixed.
use_cases.move: Say that the authors call EQ the flexible one of the three traits, so it is worth practicing.

use_cases.situation: You are choosing what to improve this year.
use_cases.move: Name which of the four skills you want to work on and write down one situation where you will try it.

use_cases.situation: A friend quotes the 58% figure as proof.
use_cases.move: Point out that the number comes from the authors' company and read it as their claim.

pocket_idea: The 58% figure is TalentSmart's own, but the point stands on its own: EQ is the one of the three traits you can still train.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The book says IQ and personality barely move, EQ does, and its own company's data puts 58% of job performance on EQ.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Bradberry and Greaves split a person into IQ, personality and EQ, say the first two mostly stay put and EQ can be trained, and cite their company's data: 58% of job performance, and 90% of top performers high in EQ. It is company data, not independent research.
